title: Buena Vista Social Club

sections.content: Wim Wenders follows American guitarist Ry Cooder to Havana, where he reunites an extraordinary group of forgotten Cuban musicians, many in their 70s and 80s, to record an album that would become a global sensation. The film captures these artists not just performing, but sharing their lives, memories, and the soul of Cuban music.

The film transcends its role as a music documentary to become a vital document of Cuban culture during a period of isolation. Like Paris, Texas (1984), another Wenders masterpiece, it explores themes of rediscovery and connection. The film parallels other great music documentaries like The Last Waltz (1978) in its ability to capture a pivotal musical moment.

Within the music documentary genre, Buena Vista Social Club stands apart for its patient, observational style. Unlike the more confrontational approach of Don't Look Back (1967) or the concert-focused Stop Making Sense (1984), Wenders creates a gentle, immersive experience.
The film influenced later works like 20 Feet from Stardom (2013) and Searching for Sugar Man (2012) in its focus on overlooked musical talents, helping spark a renewed interest in world music.
